parent_objective: convert the gate utility matrix into an active gate policy for daily engineering paper-route proof and extended regression
blocked_by: M1185 recommends classifications but does not define how daily gates promotion gates and extended-regression gates should be scheduled
supersedes: ambiguous use of all historical gates as either always-active blockers or disposable legacy artifacts
invalidates: deleting historical tools during policy design
using Stack A as proof of self-identification
using Stack C as a permanent blocker for every finite-window or engineering baseline

public_gates: M1186 may write active gate policy documents only
M1186 must not run candidate replay
M1186 must not delete historical gates
M1186 must not train actor weights
M1186 must not use private holdout
M1186 must not change actor inputs
forbidden_shortcuts: do not claim driver performance from policy design
do not claim recurrent belief from gate policy

workflow_synthesis.evidence_axis: G_process: active gate policy from utility matrix
workflow_synthesis.evidence_increment: turns the M1185 provisional matrix into a written scheduling policy for core daily balanced public and extended historical diagnostics
workflow_synthesis.claim_scope: process policy only; no replay result gate deletion training PPO promotion private-holdout driver-performance or paper-result claim
stop_condition: stop if policy deletes historical gates without a separate implementation milestone
stop if policy treats Stack A as sufficient self-ID proof
stop if policy keeps Stack C as an unconditional blocker for every future controller comparison
stop if policy changes actor inputs
fallback_plan: if matrix evidence is insufficient, route to candidate inventory or executable gate audit
if Stack B is under-specified, write a Stack B executable wrapper design before controller comparisons
if a Stack C gate has unique coverage, keep it as extended-regression or core with explicit trigger conditions
workflow_synthesis.synthesis_trigger: M1185 matrix is complete enough to define active daily and extended gate policy before L0/L1/L2/L3 controller comparison design

admission_evidence: M1185 matrix classifies gates as core research-only extended-regression legacy and deprecated
Stack A is insufficient for proof but needed for engineering behavior
Stack B is recommended as current paper-route default
Stack C remains valuable as extended regression rather than unconditional blocker
allowed_updates: status, queue, scoreboard, research log, and review artifacts
next_stage_criteria: legacy and deprecated handling is defined
next paper-route controller-comparison design is pre-registered

self_id_evidence_discipline.current_frame_substitution_risk: M1186 writes process policy and does not test current-frame substitution or history necessity.
self_id_evidence_discipline.negative_result_policy: If the active gate policy cannot separate engineering behavior from mechanism proof, route to executable gate audit before controller comparison.
allowed_claims: no self-identification, driver capability, promotion, private-holdout, real-vehicle, or paper-result claim

hypothesis: The M1185 gate utility matrix is sufficient to define an active gate policy that protects engineering behavior, public proof, and extended historical diagnostics without letting old row-specific gates dominate the paper route.
success_criteria: daily core gate policy is defined
balanced public gate policy is defined
legacy and deprecated handling policy is defined
follow-up controller comparison design is pre-registered
no candidate replay, gate deletion, actor training, PPO, promotion, private holdout, or actor-input change occurs
failure_criteria: policy deletes gates instead of scheduling them
policy treats Stack A as sufficient mechanism proof
policy keeps Stack C as unconditional blocker for all future controller comparisons
follow-up controller comparison is not pre-registered
candidate replay, actor training, PPO, promotion, private holdout, or actor-input change starts

commands.name: write_active_gate_policy
commands.command: write docs/active-gate-policy.md and docs/m1186-paper-route-active-gate-policy-design.md from the M1185 utility matrix

decision_rule: M1186 passes if it defines the active gate policy and pre-registers the L0/L1/L2/L3 controller comparison design without changing gates or running experiments.
